termDefinitions.meaningEn: A commit log records changes before they're applied to the in-memory structure — here, BigTable's WAL.

termDefinitions.meaning: BigTable 按 row 范围切分出的服务单位，一个 server 管很多个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tablet is a row-range slice of a BigTable table; one server manages many.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多笔小写合并成一次 fsync，摊薄持久化成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Group commit batches many small writes into a single fsync to amortize durability cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志条目的递增序号，用于恢复时按顺序重放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSN is the monotonically increasing sequence number of a log entry, used to replay logs in order during recovery.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 的分布式文件系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GFS is Google's distributed file system.

optionExplanations: 论文原因：每个 tablet 各开一份 GFS 文件等于把顺序写拆成几千份并发小写。
这恰恰是选单份 log 之后必须付的代价，不是它要避免的问题，选项把因果说反了。
memtable 按 tablet 独立管理，和 commit log 是几份没有关系。
Chubby 连接数和 commit log 份数是两件独立的事，论文没有绑在一起。
optionExplanations_en: The paper's own reason: one GFS file per tablet turns sequential writes into thousands of concurrent small writes.
This is exactly the cost paid for choosing a single log, not the problem it avoids — the option reverses cause and effect.
Each tablet manages its own memtable independently; that has nothing to do with how many log files exist.
Chubby connection count and commit log count are separate concerns the paper never ties together.

scenario: 面试官追问：「都用 NVMe SSD 了，4KB 随机读大概 100 微秒，你这套避免随机 I/O 的逻辑过时了吗？」你的系统跑在云上，数据盘是网络挂载的块存储。
scenario_en: The interviewer pushes back: "Everyone uses NVMe SSD now — a 4KB random read takes about 100 microseconds. Isn't your whole avoid-random-I/O logic outdated?" Your system runs in the cloud on network-attached block storage.
q: 该怎么回应“SSD 时代顺序化还重要吗”？
q_en: How should you respond to "does sequential I/O still matter in the SSD era"?
options: 承认已经过时：SSD 没有磁头，随机读和顺序读速度已经完全一样
结论不变，理由换成：小随机写在 SSD 内部也有写放大、每次 I/O 有固定开销、网络盘上一次 I/O 是一次网络往返
只承认一半：本地 SSD 上确实不重要了，但这和分布式存储完全无关
回避理由，直接说：工业界现在都还在用 LSM，所以肯定有用
options_en: Admit it's outdated — SSDs have no seek head, so random and sequential reads now cost exactly the same.

Keep the conclusion, with new reasons: small random writes still cause write amplification inside the SSD, every I/O has fixed overhead, and on network-attached disks each I/O is a network round trip.
Half-concede: it stopped mattering on local SSDs, but that's unrelated to distributed storage.
Dodge the reasoning and just say the industry still runs LSM everywhere, so it must still matter.
whenOtherWins: 若负载读多、要范围扫描和可预测 p99，写的也不是随机 key，即使在 SSD 上 B-tree 依然更合适。
tradeoff: B-tree 原地更新、读路径短，但小更新要改写整页；LSM 把写顺序化、靠后台 compaction 付写放大和读放大。SSD 降低了随机读代价，但没有消掉这个权衡。
why: SSD 没有寻道，但 NAND 只能按 page 写、按 erase block 擦，小随机写会触发 FTL 垃圾回收，设备内写放大更大、磨损更快；每次 I/O 还有固定的命令和中断开销，零散小 I/O 摊不薄；题面说数据盘是网络挂载块存储，一次 I/O 是一次网络往返，延迟和按 IOPS 计费都让「攒成大块顺序写」更划算。结论不变，只是理由从「磁头寻道」换成了这三条。
why_en: SSDs have no seek, but NAND writes by page and erases by block, so small random writes trigger FTL garbage collection, adding device-level write amplification and wear; every I/O also carries fixed command overhead; and on the network-attached block storage given in the scenario, each I/O is a network round trip with IOPS-based limits and pricing. The conclusion holds — only the reasons change from disk seeks to these three.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无磁头的固态盘，随机读延迟约 100 微秒。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An NVMe SSD is a headless flash drive with roughly 100-microsecond random read latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 磁盘/SSD 最小 I/O 单位，通常 4KB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A page is the smallest I/O unit on disk or SSD, typically 4KB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位延迟，衡量最慢那 1% 请求的表现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 is the 99th-percentile latency, measuring how the slowest 1% of requests perform.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨网络发起的一次调用，云存储上一次 I/O 本质是一次 RPC。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An RPC is a call made across the network; on cloud storage, one I/O is essentially one RPC.

optionExplanations: 随机读延迟从 10ms 降到约 100µs，但“完全一样”和 page 粒度读放大的事实不符。
把结论和支撑理由拆开——结论没变，但理由换成了 SSD 与网络盘时代的版本：写放大、固定 I/O 开销、网络往返。
本地 SSD 上小随机写仍有写放大，每次 I/O 也有固定开销，这两条和分布式无关，不能只认一半。
不给理由的回答最先在追问环节垮——面试官下一句就是“为什么”。
optionExplanations_en: Random-read latency dropped from 10ms to ~100µs, but "identical" ignores page-level read amplification.
Separate the conclusion from its support — the conclusion holds, but the reasons are now the SSD and network-disk versions: write amplification, fixed I/O overhead, network round trips.
Even on local SSDs, small random writes cause write amplification and every I/O has fixed overhead; those two are unrelated to distribution, so you can't concede only half.
An answer with no reasoning collapses at the first follow-up, which is always "why."

scenario: 团队想把跑了很久的 MapReduce 批处理换成 Spark，理由是“MapReduce 太老该淘汰了”。
scenario_en: A team wants to replace a long-running MapReduce batch pipeline with Spark, reasoning that "MapReduce is old and should be retired."
q: Spark/Flink 抛弃了 MapReduce 的什么，又留下了什么？
q_en: What did Spark/Flink drop from MapReduce, and what did they keep?
options: 抛弃了按 key 分组这件事，换成纯内存哈希表，从此不再排序数据
抛弃了失败就重跑的容错思路，换成同步复制好几份副本
抛弃每步都把结果落 HDFS，stage 内走内存流水线；按 key 聚合仍要 shuffle 重分布（常伴随排序或溢写排序）
抛弃了把计算搬到数据旁边调度的思路，从此不再关心本地性
options_en: Dropped key-based grouping entirely for a pure in-memory hash table, so data is no longer sorted at all.
Dropped re-run-on-failure fault tolerance for synchronously copying several replicas instead.
Dropped writing every step's output to HDFS for in-memory pipelining within a stage; key-based aggregation still needs a shuffle (often with sorting or sort-on-spill).
Dropped scheduling compute next to data, and no longer cares about locality at all.
why: Spark/Flink 用 DAG 把多步串成流水线，不再每步都写 HDFS 三副本；但只要按 key 聚合，就仍要 shuffle 把数据按 key 重分布，Spark 的 sort-based shuffle 和溢写都会排序——这是「分组靠重分布+排序」的现代延续，不是原样照搬。容错上 Spark 靠 lineage 重算丢失分区，Flink 靠 checkpoint 快照恢复，都不是同步多副本；本地性调度两者都保留。
why_en: Spark/Flink pipeline steps as a DAG instead of writing every step to triple-replicated HDFS, but key-based aggregation still needs a shuffle to redistribute data by key, and Spark's sort-based shuffle and spills still sort — a modern continuation, not an unchanged copy. For fault tolerance Spark recomputes lost partitions from lineage and Flink restores from checkpoints; neither uses synchronous replicas. Both keep locality-aware scheduling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有向无环图，dataflow 引擎的执行计划形状。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DAG is a directed acyclic graph — the shape of a dataflow engine's execution plan.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把中间数据按 key 搬运并排序、送到对应下游任务的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shuffle is the phase that sorts intermediate data by key and delivers it to the matching downstream task.

termDefinitions.meaning: 失败时根据算子依赖关系从可用输入重新计算丢失分区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lineage recovery recomputes a lost partition from available inputs using the operator dependency graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源版 GFS，Hadoop/MapReduce 的默认存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HDFS is the open-source GFS equivalent, the default storage for Hadoop/MapReduce.

optionExplanations: 内存放不下时，哈希聚合一样要溢出成排序，“不再排序”这个说法不成立。
Spark 靠 lineage 重算、Flink 靠 checkpoint 恢复，都不是同步复制多副本，选项把方向说反了。
DAG 流水线不强制每步写 HDFS 三副本，但按 key 聚合时仍要 shuffle 重分布，常伴随排序或溢写排序。
本地性调度在 Spark/Flink 里依然存在，不是被抛弃的部分。
optionExplanations_en: When memory runs out, hash aggregation spills and becomes a sort anyway, so "no longer needed" doesn't hold.
Spark recomputes from lineage and Flink restores from checkpoints; neither uses synchronous multi-replica copying, so the option has the direction backwards.
A DAG pipeline doesn't force every step to write triple-replicated HDFS, but key-based aggregation still needs a shuffle, often with sorting or sort-on-spill.
Locality-aware scheduling is still present in Spark/Flink; it was never dropped.

scenario: Lucene/ES 的 segment：不可变、稀疏 term index、postings、merge、tombstone 删除——和 SSTable 几乎一一对应，却独立开发。
scenario_en: Lucene/Elasticsearch's segment design — immutable, a sparse term index, a postings file, merges, tombstone deletes — maps almost one-to-one onto SSTable, yet was built completely independently.
q: 这种跨系统结构收敛，最合理的解释是？
q_en: What best explains this cross-system structural convergence?
options: Lucene 的作者当年直接借鉴了 BigTable 论文里的开源实现代码
纯粹是巧合，两者除了名字相似之外没有实质相同的设计逻辑
因为两者都跑在 JVM 上，受同一套垃圾回收机制约束才趋同
负载都是“按 key 查一串值”且超内存，才收敛出同一种存储形状
options_en: Lucene's authors directly copied the open-source implementation described in the BigTable paper.
Purely a coincidence — beyond similar names, the two share no real design logic.
Both run on the JVM, and the same garbage collector constraints pushed them to converge.
Both workloads look like 'find a run of values by key' and outgrow memory, so they converge on the same shape.
why: 寻道贵、顺序读便宜这个物理事实不挑团队和语言；只要负载是“按 key 找一串值”且放不进内存，就会收敛出同一种形状。
why_en: The physical fact that seeks are expensive and sequential reads are cheap doesn't care about team or language, so any workload shaped like 'look up a run of values by key' that outgrows memory converges on the same shape.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 的不可变数据文件单位，等价于 SSTable。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A segment is Lucene's immutable data-file unit, the equivalent of an SSTable.

termDefinitions.meaning: Lucene 内存里的稀疏词典索引，指向 postings 文件的偏移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The term index is Lucene's in-memory sparse dictionary index, pointing to offsets in the postings file.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存实际倒排列表数据的文件，对应 SSTable 的 block。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postings is the file holding the actual inverted-list data, analogous to an SSTable's blocks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标记删除的墓碑记录，真正回收发生在 merge/compaction 时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone marks a deletion; actual space reclamation happens during merge or compaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: Java 字节码运行环境。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The JVM is the runtime that executes Java bytecode.

optionExplanations: Lucene 诞生早于 2006 年 BigTable 论文公开，时间线对不上，借鉴关系不成立。
结构点逐一对应（segment↔SSTable、term index↔稀疏索引、merge↔compaction），不只是名字像。
LevelDB/RocksDB 用 C++ 写、不跑 JVM，同样是这个形状，说明 GC 不是驱动因素。
物理约束不挑语言/团队，能解释为什么诞生时间、实现语言都不同的系统会长成一个样子。
optionExplanations_en: Lucene predates the 2006 BigTable paper's publication, so the timeline rules out direct borrowing.
The structural points map one-to-one (segment/SSTable, term index/sparse index, merge/compaction) — more than a naming coincidence.
LevelDB and RocksDB are C++ and never touch the JVM, yet share the same shape, so GC isn't the driver.
A shared physical constraint doesn't care about language or team, explaining convergence across different eras and stacks.

scenario: 面试题：“设计离线系统，每天从 10 亿条日志算出访问量 Top 1000 的 URL”，数据放不进单机内存，允许分钟级延迟。
scenario_en: The prompt: "design an offline system that computes the top 1,000 URLs by traffic from 1 billion log lines every day", data too big for one machine's memory, minutes of delay acceptable.
q: 哪些信号提示该用 MapReduce 风格方案？
q_en: Which signals point you toward a MapReduce-style design?
options: 按 key 聚合、单机内存放不下、能容忍批处理延迟，三者同时具备才算
只要题目提到“日志”两个字，不管其他约束都该默认用 MapReduce
只要数据量是“10 亿”这种大数字，不管是否要按 key 聚合都该套用
只要允许延迟，不管数据量多大，都该优先考虑 MapReduce 方案
options_en: Key-based aggregation, memory-exceeding data, and tolerable batch latency — only counts when all three hold together.
Whenever the prompt says "logs", regardless of other constraints, default straight to MapReduce.
Whenever the number is huge like "1 billion", regardless of whether key aggregation is needed, apply it anyway.
Whenever latency is tolerable, regardless of data size, MapReduce should be the first choice considered.
whenOtherWins: 若同样是聚合但要秒级更新的实时排行榜，该换流式增量聚合（如 Flink 滑动窗口）；MapReduce 式整批重跑延迟太高。
tradeoff: MapReduce 整批重算胜在简单、天然容错 vs 流式增量聚合胜在低延迟但状态管理更复杂
why: 单个信号都不够，要“按 key 聚合+内存放不下+能接受批延迟”同时成立，才说明问题形状是 sort-then-group，不是随便套 MapReduce。
why_en: No single clue is enough — key-based aggregation, data too big for memory, and tolerance for batch latency all have to hold at once before the problem actually matches MapReduce's sort-then-group shape.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先排序制造 key 相邻、再顺序扫描分组的处理形状。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sort-then-group is the pattern of sorting to create key adjacency, then scanning sequentially to group by key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 整批数据一次性处理完再出结果，允许分钟到小时级延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batch processing runs over a whole dataset at once and tolerates minutes-to-hours of latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理框架，支持滑动窗口做增量聚合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream-processing framework that supports sliding-window incremental aggregation.

optionExplanations: 三个约束合在一起，才把问题锁定成“先排序制造相邻、再顺序扫描分组”这一种形状。
“日志”只说明数据来源，不说明是否要按 key 聚合，单靠关键词判断会误用。
数据量大只说明需要分布式，不说明该用批处理还是流处理，这是正交维度。
延迟容忍只是“可以用批处理”的必要条件之一，不是“必须用 MapReduce”的充分条件。
optionExplanations_en: Only all three together lock the problem into "sort to create adjacency, then scan sequentially to group."
"Logs" only describes the data source, not whether key aggregation is needed; keying off one word misfires.
A huge data volume only implies you need distribution, not whether to pick batch or streaming — an orthogonal axis.
Latency tolerance is one necessary condition for batch being viable, not sufficient proof MapReduce is required.

scenario: 面试官明说“不能用现成数据库或索引，自己实现”，同时数据量远超内存、查询要按某字段随机查找。
scenario_en: The interviewer explicitly says "no off-the-shelf database or index — build it yourself", while data volume far exceeds memory and queries need random lookups on a field.
q: 听到“不许用数据库”，第一句该说什么？
q_en: When you hear "no database allowed", what should your first sentence be?
options: 直接说要维护一份内存哈希表，把整个数据集都塞进单机内存里
先说清优化目标——同 key 数据磁盘连续，一次寻道加一段顺序读
直接说按行号给数据建索引，查询时靠行号逐步跳转定位记录
先问面试官能不能改用 Redis 来代替，试图绕开这条已经说明的限制
options_en: Jump straight to an in-memory hash table holding the whole dataset on one machine.
State the optimization target first — same-key data contiguous on disk, one seek plus one sequential read.
Jump straight to indexing by line number, jumping to a record via its line.
Ask upfront whether Redis is allowed, trying to route around the restriction.
whenOtherWins: 若数据量小到能塞进单机内存、且不要求持久化，直接上内存哈希表更简单，不必大费周章讲 SSTable。
tradeoff: 先讲目标再讲实现换来“被追问单点细节不会整体崩” vs 开场多花几秒钟报清楚约束
why: 先说优化目标，后面无论用偏移量还是稀疏索引来实现，面试官戳中一个细节也不会让整个方案崩；直接跳到实现是这类题最容易翻车的地方。
why_en: State the optimization target first — disk locality, one seek plus one sequential read — so any single implementation detail the interviewer pokes at can be swapped without collapsing the whole answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让常一起被访问的数据在磁盘上物理相邻，减少 I/O 次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Disk locality means keeping commonly co-accessed data physically adjacent on disk to cut the number of I/Os.

termDefinitions.meaning: 磁盘/文件定位到某个字节偏移的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A seek is the operation of positioning a read at a given byte offset in a file.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文件内以字节为单位的位置，是 seek() 真正接受的参数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A byte offset is a position within a file measured in bytes — the actual parameter seek() accepts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有序、不可变、带稀疏索引的文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is a sorted, immutable file with a sparse index.

optionExplanations: 数据量远超内存这个前提下，内存哈希表直接不成立。
先说目标能让后续任何实现细节都变成“实现这个目标的一种方式”，被戳中一处不会全盘崩。
行号不是磁盘地址，seek() 只接受字节偏移，跳到第 N 行本质还是要扫完前面。
题目已明说不能用数据库/索引，Redis 属同类被禁工具，绕限制显得没理解题意。
optionExplanations_en: An in-memory hash table is a non-starter given the stated premise that data exceeds memory.
Stating the target first turns every later implementation detail into 'one way to hit this target', so one poke doesn't collapse it all.
A line number isn't a disk address; seek() only takes byte offsets, so reaching line N still means scanning everything before it.
The prompt already ruled out databases and indexes; Redis is the same category of banned tool, and asking for it signals missing the point.
